turboprop.propeller_compressibility_source: Propeller class: the FH385/FH386 is an eight-blade high-speed design for a maximum flight Mach number of 0.72 (Schirmer, H., Dostal, H., Modern Turboprop Control for the TP400-D6 Engine Powering the A400M, DGLR-2006-094, Deutscher Luft- und Raumfahrtkongress 2006, p. 1), the advanced thin-blade class of the NASA high-speed propeller programme, not the conventional thick-blade class (5 to 7 percent thick at 75 percent radius) whose efficiency falls rapidly above Mach 0.5 (Mitchell, G. A., Mikkelson, D. C., Summary and Recent Results from the NASA Advanced High-Speed Propeller Research Program, NASA TM-82891, 1982, p. 2). Coefficient from the same report, pp. 5-6 (wind-tunnel net efficiency of the eight-blade models at constant power coefficient and advance ratio 3.06, Mach 0.6 to 0.85, so the helical tip Mach number is 1.433 M): the 45 deg swept blade exceeded 81 percent at Mach 0.6 to 0.7 with a 2 to 3 point advantage over the straight blade, and gave 78.7 percent at Mach 0.8 (M_h 1.147), 3 points above the straight blade. The straight blade, the conservative bound because no FH386 sweep is published, therefore holds 78.5 percent at Mach 0.65 (M_h 0.932) and 75.7 percent at Mach 0.8: a ratio 0.964, which the model's form 1 - c (M_h - 0.89)^2 at its unchanged onset 0.89 meets with c = 0.556 (0.46 to 0.65 for 78.0 to 79.0 percent at Mach 0.65; 0.44 if the 3 percent is relative). The generic class value 4 (no retrieved source) stays for propellers that state none.
turboprop.power_lapse_source: Flat-rating corner, derived: EASA TCDS E.033 Issue 08 states the ratings at sea level ISA on a test bed (Note 6) under one TGT limit, 997 C, for maximum take-off and maximum continuous (IV.1.2), and prints no flat-rating temperature. Jane's All the World's Aircraft (2008-2009 ed.), Airbus A400M, power plant, p. 296: 9,694 kW (13,000 shp) thermodynamic power de-rated for take-off. The corner is where that thermodynamic power, lapsed by the exponent below, falls to the 7,971 kW normal take-off and maximum-continuous rating: sigma = (7971/9694)^(1/0.728) = 0.7643 (ISA about 8,900 ft), entered as the sea-level temperature of the model's corner form, 288.15 K / 0.7643 = 377.02 K; it is a density corner, not an ambient temperature limit. The same thermodynamic power sets every rating's corner (thermodynamic_shaft_power_kw): a flat-rated engine holds a rating while its gas generator, lapsing, can still make it, and follows the thermodynamic line beyond (Torenbeek, Synthesis of Subsonic Airplane Design (1982), Sec. 4.4, Fig. 4-41, p. 134), so the corner of a rating P is sigma = (P/9694)^(1/0.728): normal take-off and maximum continuous 0.7643 (ISA about 8,900 ft), uprated take-off 8,251 kW 0.8014 (about 7,400 ft), maximum climb 7,059.6 kW 0.6469 (about 14,200 ft), maximum cruise 6,866.3 kW 0.6227 (about 15,300 ft); above its corner each rating reads 9,694 kW sigma^0.728 times the ram factor. Density exponent: NO TP400 SOURCE; 0.728 is the PW120 fit of Nita (2008) eq. 3.5.11 along a constant 275 kt; with the ram factor of ram_power_source taken relative to that schedule, the thermodynamic line read at a fixed Mach lapses as sigma^0.75 to sigma^0.76 between 8,000 and 12,000 m. Class band: Torenbeek, Synthesis of Subsonic Airplane Design (1982), Sec. 5.4.3, eq. (5-70), p. 165: power at altitude over power at sea level = sigma^n 'for a given rating and Mach number', 'n is generally between .7 and .8', for an engine with no structural or thermal limitation up to some altitude (the flat-rated part is the corner above); the line is inside it. No retrieved source supports a weaker lapse: Raymer, Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach (6th ed., 2018), App. E.3, p. 993 (Mattingly-cycle 6,500 hp turboprop): the full-throttle airflow at Mach 0 follows delta/sqrt(theta) from sea level to 30,000 ft (41 to 13.8 lb/s), a constant corrected gas-generator point, so its static power lapses as delta sqrt(theta), about sigma^1.35 at 30,000 ft (its full-throttle thrust at M 0.85, times the speed of sound ratio at constant propeller efficiency, gives a fixed-Mach power exponent referred to sea level of about 0.6 at 10,000 ft, 0.7 at 20,000 ft and 0.9 at 30,000 ft, about 1.25 locally between 20,000 and 30,000 ft); Sadraey, Aircraft Design: A Systems Engineering Approach (2012), eq. (8.16), p. 462 suggests m = 1.2 for a turboprop. Climb and cruise power shares: NO TP400 SOURCE (see rating_source); the corners above are static; with the ram factor each rating holds its flat value higher, the maximum climb to about 6,100 m (20,000 ft) at 220 KIAS and 7,500 to 8,200 m (24,600 to 26,800 ft) at Mach 0.65 to 0.72, the maximum cruise to 7,800 to 8,500 m (25,600 to 27,900 ft) at Mach 0.65 to 0.72, so the shares enter the Mach climb and a cruise up to about FL280 and every rating reads the thermodynamic line above it. Rating temperature limit 288.15 K: no TP400-D6 flat-rating temperature is printed in EASA TCDS E.033 Issue 08, the MTU Aero Engines TP400-D6 brochure (11,000 shp at sea level), the Europrop International TP400-D6 page or Jane's 2008-2009, so every rating, the 8,251 kW uprated take-off included, is held at its full value only to the TCDS rating condition, sea level ISA under the TGT limit (Note 6), and lapses as (288.15 K / T)^n above it; the density corner still applies on a cold day at altitude
turboprop.psfc_source: Kaiser, S., Donnerhack, S., Lundbladh, A., Seitz, A., A Composite Cycle Engine Concept with Hecto-Pressure Ratio, AIAA 2015-4028 (51st AIAA/SAE/ASEE Joint Propulsion Conference, 2015), Table 1, p. 3: Europrop TP400 (2009), cruise, 0.35 lbm/eshp-hr, citing Jane's Aero Engines 2013/2014; = 0.2129 kg/(kW h) (1 lbm = 0.45359237 kg, 1 shp = 0.745699872 kW). The figure is per equivalent shaft power (exhaust thrust included); this installation declares no residual jet thrust, so the propeller shaft power carries the equivalent power and the figure is burned on it. ASSUMED reference temperature: the cruise condition is not stated; 216.65 K is ISA at the A400M's declared cruise level, 11,278 m (37,000 ft, the top of the long-range-cruise band in Jane's All the World's Aircraft (2008-2009 ed.), Airbus A400M, p. 296); at FL250 instead (238.62 K) the burned PSFC would be 4.7 % lower
turboprop.ram_power_source: Ram exponent 3.45, read from Nita (2008, HAW Hamburg, ATR 72 design study) Fig. 3.6, p. 38, maximum cruise power of the PW120 against true airspeed at 5,000-30,000 ft (from McCormick 1995): a least-squares fit of P = P0 (1 + 0.2 M^2)^k to each digitised curve (M from the ISA speed of sound) gives k = 3.40 (5,000 ft, to 240 kt, below the 1,620 shp limit), 3.62 (10,000), 3.41 (15,000), 3.49 (20,000), 3.36 (25,000) and 3.43 (30,000 ft); mean 3.45. Reading uncertainty +/-0.15: the spread between curves, against about +/-0.08 for one pixel (1.8 shp) at the two ends of a curve. The form is the corrected-parameter similarity of Torenbeek, Advanced Aircraft Design (1st ed., 2013), eq. 3.30, p. 69, P / (delta sqrt(theta)) = f(N / sqrt(theta), M), and Torenbeek, Synthesis of Subsonic Airplane Design (1982), eq. 5-70, p. 165 (lapse for a given rating and Mach number); its ideal upper bound is (3.5 + 0.5) = 4, which neither book prints. NO TP400 SOURCE: the PW120 chart is the class value. The density exponent borrowed from Nita (2008) eq. 3.5.11 was fitted along the same chart at 275 kt = 141.472 m/s true airspeed (Fig. 3.7), so the factor is taken relative to that schedule (no double count). The rating caps the result. The climb and cruise shares copied from the PW127M (rating_source) are the ATR 72-600 factsheet's maximum climb and maximum cruise power limits (2,192 and 2,132 shp), listed with the static take-off and maximum-continuous ratings and stated at no speed: rating caps, so ram is not counted in them. Class check: Raymer, Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach (6th ed., 2018), App. E.3, p. 993 (6,500 hp turboprop, uninstalled full-throttle thrust, chart digitised) gives about 3,490 lb at 25,000 ft M 0.7, a thrust power of 0.69 of its sea-level static shaft power

ESTIMATES, not published: maximum climb and maximum cruise shaft power are the PW127M catalogue fractions of normal take-off power (1634.574/1845.607 = 0.88566 and 1589.832/1845.607 = 0.86141) applied to 7971 kW; maximum_cruise_fuel_flow_kg_h is a TWO-engine figure (FUEL_FLOW_REFERENCE_ENGINES = 2) equal to 2 x the PW127M power-specific fuel consumption (762/2 kg/h over 1589.832 kW = 0.23965 kg/kWh) x 6866.3 kW; it only feeds the fuel validation report, the model burns the PSFC of psfc_source; no TP400-D6 climb or cruise rating is public. 1 shp = 0.745699872 kW
